info.title: castor API
info.description: The API behind the 學益 webapp. Generated from the backend_new route definitions by tools/openapi.ts -- do not edit by hand.

amount.description: NTD. The authoritative price: a client must render this, never a constant of its own

days.description: Days of access, added to whatever the caller already has

maxedSpiritCount.description: Spirits grown to max level -- every one of them is owed

confirmedAmount.description: Summed from the frozen per-donation amounts

pendingCount.description: Maxed, but the owner has not picked an organisation yet

pendingAmount.description: pendingCount x donationAmount -- the only figure here priced at today's rate

promisedAmount.description: confirmedAmount + pendingAmount, so a reader can check it

transferredAmount.description: Over published batches only, so the listed batches add up to it

donationAmount.description: Today's figure, which prices pendingAmount and nothing else

reference.description: Bank transaction number, or the last digits of the account

donationUnitAmount.description: The one frozen amount every member shares, or null when they differ; null means the multiplication must not be printed

platformTopUp.description: transferredAmount - donationSubtotal. Signed: negative would mean the batch sent less than was promised

total.description: Rows matching the query, ignoring limit and offset

totalPages.description: At least 1, so an empty result reads as "page 1 of 1" rather than "of 0"

attemptCount.description: How many times the questions were practised -- a 題組 answered once counts once

questionCount.description: Servable top-level questions, counted as in /stats

exams.description: Ranked like the subjects themselves, and empty when none of them is filed under an exam

parentId.description: The option this one hangs under, or null for a top-level option

code.description: Stable identifier, and what ties a spirit species to this category

isActive.description: Inactive categories stay listed -- past donations point at them and the public record keeps naming them. They drop out of the picker only.

taxId.description: The 統編. Null for associations that do not publish one

categories.description: Ordered by the category sortOrder, then id. Never empty: at least one is required

lifetimePoints.description: Only ever increases; the leaderboard ranks on this

active.description: Whether an agreement period is in status `active`. A billing fact, not an access one.

expiresAt.description: ISO 8601 end of the active period, or null when there is none

entitled.description: Whether paid features are available right now. The field to gate subscriber-only UI on: a cancelled agreement inside the period it already paid for reports active:false and entitled:true.

autoRenew.description: Whether anything will charge the card again. Not derivable from entitlement -- a day pass grants access with no agreement behind it.

amount.description: Frozen at checkout, so a re-priced plan never rewrites it

choosePayment.description: One of Credit, ATM, CVS, BARCODE

status.description: One of created, awaiting, paid, expired, failed. `created` is a form handed to the browser with nothing reserved; `awaiting` means ECPay issued a code or virtual account and **the money has not arrived** -- where an ATM, CVS or BARCODE row spends most of its life; `paid`, `expired` and `failed` are terminal

paymentType.description: ECPay's expanded value, e.g. ATM_TAISHIN. Null until paid

bankCode.description: ATM only. Null for every other method

vAccount.description: ATM only -- the virtual account to transfer to

paymentNo.description: Convenience-store code. Null for every other method

barcode1.description: Store barcode, first of three segments. ECPay returns the digits only -- rendering them as a scannable Code39 barcode is the client job

expireAt.description: ISO 8601. When the code stops being payable; null before one is issued

grantedUntil.description: ISO 8601. What the subscription was extended to; null until paid

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, the calendar date stored in the row

categories.description: Every category the subject belongs to, name-sorted. Subject names are not unique -- two exams can both have a 數學 -- so the category is what tells them apart. Empty for a subject filed under no category

retention.description: Probability the concept is still recallable now, 0-1. Exponential decay since the last attempt, with a strength that grows with how well it was known

level.description: retention < 0.5 is high, < 0.75 is medium, otherwise low

categories.description: Every category the subject belongs to, name-sorted. Subject names are not unique -- two exams can both have a 數學 -- so the category is what tells them apart. Empty for a subject filed under no category

platformMedianMs.description: null until the subject has enough samples platform-wide

deltaMs.description: userMedianMs - platformMedianMs, or null whenever the comparison would be unsound: no platform median yet, or fewer than five timed answers of the caller own

accuracy.description: 0-100. Reported beside speed, because fast is only good news if the answers were right

sampleCount.description: Timed answers the median was taken over

type.description: GROUP, SINGLE, MULTIPLE, TRUE_FALSE, FILL or CLOZE. Every write validates against those six; the column is a varchar, so a reader should not assume it

childCount.description: Sub-questions under this one -- how the admin sees a 題組 holds more than its stem

categories.description: The subject's category names. An array because subject-to-category is many-to-many, and empty for a subject filed under none

fbPostId.description: The Facebook post this was published as, which is what the 討論區 link is built from. Only ever set on a top-level question: facebookPoster renders a group and its children into one image and writes the id back to the parent, so a child reads its parent

type.description: GROUP, SINGLE, MULTIPLE, TRUE_FALSE, FILL or CLOZE. Every write validates against those six; the column is a varchar, so a reader should not assume it

answer.description: The answer key. Present on every read of this shape -- see AGENTS.md

adjustedDifficulty.description: Moves with how people actually score; a group averages its children

children.description: Empty unless this is a 題組; the children of one carry the questions

type.description: GROUP, SINGLE, MULTIPLE, TRUE_FALSE, FILL or CLOZE. Every write validates against those six; the column is a varchar, so a reader should not assume it

enabled.description: The admin review gate. Only enabled questions are ever served by GET /adaptive, so anything the practice UI sees has this true; the admin list shows both

attempCount.description: Misspelled to match the column. How many times this was practised

repliedAt.description: ISO 8601. Every reply from one POST shares it, which is half of what identifies a history row

parentQuestion.description: The 題組 these answers belong to, or null for a standalone question

subject.description: Id and name only -- the practice page resolves anything more from its own list

id.description: The group key: the parent's question id, or the question's own id when standalone -- in which case parentQuestion is null and entries holds exactly one

lastWrongAt.description: ISO 8601. The most recent in the group -- what the list sorts on

entries.description: In the order the sub-questions appear in the paper, not by when each went wrong

id.description: The user_wrong_question row -- what PUT /{id}/note and DELETE /{id} act on. The note is per sub-question, since that is the granularity a user writes it at

score.description: 0-10, from the most recent wrong attempt

wrongCount.description: How many times this has gone wrong

type.description: EARN_REPLY, SPEND_EGG_REDEEM and the rest -- a varchar rather than an enum, so a new kind of movement needs no schema change

replyId.description: The reply this came from, for anything earned by answering

balanceAfter.description: The running balance once this had been applied

code.description: What the frontend keys this species' artwork by

theme.description: The egg's own label, which is not the category link below

isActive.description: Whether it is still on sale; owners of a retired one keep it

category.description: The donation category this species supports, or null for one tied to none. null is both what the planned VIP spirit is and what a seeded egg looks like when its category_id was forgotten -- indistinguishable from here, which is why the admin page says it out loud.

ownersByLevel.description: Owners keyed by the level they have grown to. An absent level has no owners; the caller decides which levels to show. Keys are strings because JSON object keys are.

level.description: How far this species has been grown, or null when not owned. The collection view needs the level and not just `owned`: it shows progress per species and sorts the started ones first.

nextLevelXp.description: XP this spirit still needs for its next level, or null at the maximum

userGuardianId.description: Which maxed spirit paid for it -- how the picker knows one is spent

amount.description: Frozen at confirmation. Never render the current donationAmount in its place

published.description: Whether the public page shows this batch yet. A donation can be paid before its evidence is uploaded, and this record should not link to a batch nobody can read.

batch.description: null while the money has not gone out yet -- there is no status column

organization.description: null only if the organisation row has gone, which a FK should prevent

transferredAmount.description: What actually left the bank account

get.summary: List the subscription plans and their prices
get.description: Public and unauthenticated, because the pricing page is read before signing in. These are the authoritative amounts: the figure shown has to be the figure signed into the ECPay order, so a client must not hold prices of its own.

Every published payout, with the arithmetic a reader needs to check it against the receipt linked from its evidence: donationCount x donationUnitAmount + platformTopUp equals transferredAmount. Public and unauthenticated on purpose -- being readable by anyone is the whole of its value as proof. It names no user; a batch is the smallest unit shown.

post.description:
Behind requireUser. **Charges nothing.** It answers with a signed form the browser has to POST to `action`, because the cardholder has to reach ECPay's own page to enter a card -- the amount and the callback URLs are signed server-side so they cannot be tampered with, and the submit happens client-side. Until ECPay's webhook arrives the order is only `created`, and the user may simply close the tab.

A day pass requires `method`; the recurring plan refuses one, since ECPay's 定期定額 is credit-card only -- which is the reason the day passes exist at all. Changing recurring plan replaces the agreement, because ECPay cannot amend one: the old agreement is stopped by this call, so abandoning the payment page leaves the caller with no auto-renew. The UI has to say so before calling this.

200.description: The form to POST. Nothing has been charged

action.description: ECPay's checkout URL. POST the form here

params.description: The signed form fields, named as ECPay names them. POST every one of them verbatim: CheckMacValue signs the rest, so adding, dropping or editing a field invalidates it and ECPay rejects the order. Nothing is charged by reading this -- the cardholder has to reach ECPay's own page, and until its webhook arrives the order is only `created`

400.description: A day pass with no method (PAYMENT_METHOD_REQUIRED), or the recurring plan the caller is already on (ALREADY_SUBSCRIBED) -- the code in the body says which

get.summary: The caller's own day-pass purchases, newest first
get.description: Behind requireUser, and scoped to the caller by the query rather than by an id in the path -- there is no id to guess at. It exists because an ATM or convenience-store payer has to be able to come back for the number: they leave the site to pay, possibly days later and from another device, and the virtual account was shown once on a page they have long closed. At most 20; nobody plausibly has more.

get.summary: The subscriber-only analysis page, in one request
get.description: Behind requireUser **and** requireSubscription, and scoped to the caller. Three independent sections -- the mastery curve, the concepts most likely to have been forgotten, and answer speed against the platform -- fetched together because they share a gate and a page section. Deliberately not merged with the free GET /api/user/stats and /api/user/history: folding those in would mean demoting this route to requireUser and deciding entitlement with an `if` inside the handler, and a forgotten `if` leaks paid data silently where a forgotten middleware fails loudly.

200.description: The three sections, each possibly empty for a caller with no history

overall.description: Every subject weighted by its question count, carried forward over days with no practice

forgettingRisk.description: Most urgent first -- lowest retention, not oldest

400.description: A day range beyond 365, or a riskLimit beyond 100

get.summary: List questions for the admin catalogue
get.description: Reads in this group need no credentials: `adminAuth` gates POST/PUT/DELETE only. Top-level questions only -- a 題組's children have no meaning without their parent, and `childCount` is how the admin sees there is more to one than its stem. Paginated and filterable by category, subject, exam, concept or tag.

400.description: limit beyond the cap, or a malformed sort, order or filter

post.description: Admin only. One batch shares a subject and an exam, and commits or fails as a whole -- this route runs inside the transaction middleware, so a rejection on question N rolls back 0..N-1. Questions are created **disabled**: enabling them is PUT /{id}/enabled.

201.description: One array per submitted question, each with its children after it

schema.description: One array per submitted question, each holding the question itself followed by its children. Nested, not flat: a 題組 and its sub-questions are one submission

400.description: A malformed body, an img-placeholder left in the content, CLOZE blanks that do not match the answer, an exam not linked to the subject, or a tag or concept belonging to another subject

get.summary: How many questions match a filter
get.description: Reads in this group need no credentials: `adminAuth` gates POST/PUT/DELETE only. What the practice page shows as "questions available", so it counts only what GET /adaptive would actually serve: enabled, top-level, and a 題組 once.

total.description: Servable top-level questions matching the filters: enabled only, and a 題組 counts once. The same definition GET /api/info/stats uses

400.description: subjectId missing, or a malformed id list

get.description: Behind requireUser, on top of the group's adminAuth. Chooses by the caller's per-concept mastery, avoids what they have just seen, and marks each one pending so a second fetch before the answer lands does not hand out different work. **Every answer comes back masked** -- bullets of the same length -- because the caller has not answered yet; the history and review endpoints send the real key, this one must not.

schema.description: The chosen questions, **with every answer masked**: each is replaced by bullets of the same length, so a client can still tell whether to render an answer input and how many blanks a FILL question has, without being handed the key

400.description: subjectId missing, a malformed id list, or a count beyond 50

get.summary: Read one question, with its links and sub-questions
get.description: Reads in this group need no credentials: `adminAuth` gates POST/PUT/DELETE only. The answer key is in this response -- see AGENTS.md, where that is recorded as a known, accepted consequence of the reads here being open.

200.description: The question, its exam, tag and concept ids, and its children

fbPostId.description: Only ever set on a top-level question -- a child reads its parent

enabled.description: The admin review gate. Only enabled questions are ever served by GET /adaptive, so anything the practice UI sees has this true; the admin list shows both

type.description: GROUP, SINGLE, MULTIPLE, TRUE_FALSE, FILL or CLOZE. Every write validates against those six; the column is a varchar, so a reader should not assume it

attempCount.description: Misspelled to match the column. How many times this was practised

examId.description: A question only ever has one exam in practice, despite the M:N schema

children.description: A 題組's sub-questions, so an admin preview shows what a user is actually given. Empty for a standalone question; children carry no exam, tag or concept links of their own

put.description: Admin only. Scalar fields plus the exam. `subjectId` is deliberately not editable: tag and concept links are validated against it, and changing it would orphan them silently. Those links have their own endpoints, and so does `enabled`.

400.description: A malformed body, an img-placeholder left in the content, CLOZE blanks that do not match the answer, or an exam not linked to the subject

delete.description: Admin only. A 題組's children, and every link row pointing at it, go with it.

post.summary: Store one figure cropped out of a paper
post.description: Admin only. Returns the URL to put in the question's HTML in place of an img-placeholder-N. Nothing is written to the database, so a figure uploaded for a question that is then abandoned is an orphaned object rather than a broken row.

url.description: The stored figure's URL, to drop into the question's HTML in place of an img-placeholder-N. Nothing is written to the database: the URL only becomes part of a question when the reviewed JSON is POSTed to /api/question

400.description: An unsupported mimeType, or data that is not base64 or is oversize

get.summary: The prompt POST /image would have sent
get.description: Behind requireAdmin -- every method, not the group's adminAuth, which would let this GET through: it returns the subject's whole concept list and the full instruction text. A manual escape hatch for when the model quota is gone: paste both halves into a chat GUI with the screenshot, and the JSON that comes back drops into the same preview box the automatic path fills.

200.description: The two halves of the prompt, unjoined

userPrompt.description: Returned as two parts rather than pre-joined: a GUI with its own system-instruction field reproduces the automatic path exactly when each half goes in its own box

400.description: subjectId missing, or an imageCount out of range

404.description: No such subject, or it has no concepts to assign questions to

post.description: Admin only, and **nothing is written** -- which is why it answers 200 with no ids: the same screenshot can be re-run as many times as it takes to get a usable draft, and a human reviews and edits the result before POSTing it to /api/question. Still an array, because a 題組 plus its children is one element.

conceptIds.description: Ids the model invented are dropped, not rejected -- the admin re-picks anyway

questions.description: A draft for a human to review and edit, shaped to drop straight into POST /api/question's `questions` field. Nothing is written, which is why this is a 200 with no ids

400.description: No images, or one that is not base64 or is oversize

404.description: No such subject, or it has no concepts to assign questions to

502.description: The model answered with something that is not JSON (AI_INVALID_JSON) or does not match the expected question shape (AI_INVALID_SHAPE)

get.description: Reads in this group need no credentials: `adminAuth` gates POST/PUT/DELETE only. Ids alone: the names come from GET /api/tag.

put.description: Admin only. A full-set replace, and every tag has to belong to the question own subject.

400.description: A malformed body, or a tag belonging to another subject

put.description: Admin only. Its own endpoint rather than a field on PUT /{id}, because the admin list toggles this on a row without having the rest of the question loaded to send back.

200.description: The id and its new state

400.description: enabled missing or not a boolean

get.description: Reads in this group need no credentials: `adminAuth` gates POST/PUT/DELETE only. Ids alone: the names come from GET /api/concept.

put.description: Admin only. A full-set replace, at least one id, and every concept has to belong to the question own subject. Each concept's `numberOfQuestions` is adjusted as links are added and removed.

400.description: An empty list, or a concept belonging to another subject

post.description: Behind requireUser. One request is one submitted batch: every reply in it shares a `repliedAt`, which is what groups them into a history row. Scoring, the points award, the per-subject statistics and the wrong-question list are all written here, and a question scoring below 10 is added to that list automatically.

200.description: One result per answer submitted, in the order they were sent

correctAnswer.description: The answer key, returned so the result screen can mark the attempt

awardedPoints.description: Points actually granted, time weighting and the growth bonus included

fbPostId.description: The 討論區 link target -- a child's answer carries its parent's post id

400.description: A malformed body, or an empty batch

get.description: Behind requireUser, and scoped to the caller. **Paginated by group, not by row**: a 題組 answered in one batch is one history row, however many sub-questions it holds, so `paginate.total` counts groups. Filterable by category, subject, exam or tag -- the exam and tag links live on the top-level question, so they are matched against the group.

200.description: One page of history rows, most recently answered first

400.description: limit beyond the cap, or a malformed filter

get.description: Behind requireUser, and scoped to the caller. **Paginated by group, not by row**: a 題組 holds one row per wrong sub-question, and a flat page repeated the whole passage once per row and could split siblings across a page boundary. `paginate.total` therefore counts groups. A row whose question has since been deleted is dropped rather than rendered broken, and a group left empty goes with it. Same filters as GET /api/reply.

200.description: One page of groups, most recently wrong first

400.description: limit beyond the cap, or a malformed filter

put.summary: Write or clear the note on one wrong sub-question
put.description: Behind requireUser, and scoped to the caller: a row belonging to someone else reads as 404 rather than 403, so this never confirms that a given id exists for another user. `note: null` clears it.

200.description: The id, the note as saved, and when

updatedAt.description: ISO 8601. Always set -- this response is the write that just happened

400.description: note missing, or longer than 2000 characters

404.description: No such row belongs to this caller

delete.summary: Remove one wrong sub-question from the list
delete.description: Behind requireUser, and scoped to the caller. Answering it wrong again puts it back -- POST /api/reply re-adds anything scoring below 10.

404.description: No such row belongs to this caller

get.description: Behind requireUser, and scoped to the caller: there is no way to read anyone else's. Newest first, ordered by id rather than createdAt -- a POST /reply batch writes several rows sharing one timestamp, so id is the only column that keeps their order.

200.description: One page of movements, newest first

400.description: limit beyond the cap, or a malformed offset

get.summary: The guardian catalog, with owner counts per level
get.description: Behind requireAdmin -- every method, GET included. `adminAuth` would have been no protection at all here, since it only gates POST/PUT/DELETE and this resource has none. GET-only on purpose: a species is half a row and half a set of artwork files keyed by `code`, so creating one through an API would only ever produce a row with no pictures.

200.description: Every species, retired ones included, ordered by sortOrder then id

get.summary: The species on sale, and which of them the caller owns
get.description: Behind requireUser. Active species only, unlike the admin catalog at GET /api/species: a retired one still exists for whoever owns it, but it is not on sale.

200.description: The shelf, and the balance to spend on it

totalPoints.description: The caller's balance, so the shelf needs no second call

post.description: Behind requireUser. Spends `cost` points and hatches the egg at level 1. Only `totalPoints` is decremented, never `lifetimePoints`, so redeeming never costs leaderboard rank.

200.description: The new spirit and the balance left

id.description: The new user_guardian row, not the species

totalPoints.description: The balance after the cost was taken

400.description: Already owned (ALREADY_OWNED) or not enough points (INSUFFICIENT_POINTS) -- the code in the body says which

404.description: No such species, or it is not on sale

get.description: Every spirit this user owns, with the caller's point balance.

post.description: Spends the full `points` and adds XP, levelling the spirit up as many times as the XP covers. Paid access earns a growth bonus, which the server decides for itself from the caller's entitlement -- the request body cannot ask for it.

200.description: The spirit after the investment, the new balance, and the XP granted

xpGained.description: XP actually granted, growth bonus included

400.description: Already at the maximum level, or not enough points

404.description: No such spirit belongs to this caller

get.description: Behind requireUser, and scoped to the caller. Carries `userGuardianId` so the client can tell which of its maxed spirits have already chosen: this list and GET /api/guardian are what the picker is built from.

200.description: One page of donations, newest first by default

donationAmount.description: What confirming one more spirit would be worth. The figure a *new* donation would freeze, which is why every row above carries its own amount instead.

400.description: limit beyond the cap, or a malformed offset or order

post.summary: Confirm which organisation one maxed spirit supports
post.description: Behind requireUser. Irreversible by design: `donation.user_guardian_id` is UNIQUE, so one spirit means one donation forever. `categoryId` is required only for a species tied to no category (the VIP spirit, whose owner may direct the donation anywhere); for any other spirit the only legal value is its own category, so it can be left out.

201.description: The donation as recorded, awaiting payout

400.description: The spirit is not at the maximum level (GUARDIAN_NOT_MAX_LEVEL), it has already chosen (DONATION_ALREADY_CONFIRMED), a category is required (DONATION_CATEGORY_REQUIRED) or not its own (DONATION_CATEGORY_INVALID) or out of circulation (DONATION_CATEGORY_INACTIVE), the organisation is out of circulation (ORGANIZATION_INACTIVE) or is not offered under the chosen category (ORGANIZATION_CATEGORY_MISMATCH) -- the code in the body says which

404.description: No such spirit belongs to this caller, or no such organisation. Someone else's spirit reads as not-found rather than forbidden: whether a given id exists is not this caller's business

get.summary: What is still owed to one foundation
get.description: Admin only. The starting point of a payout: donations for this organisation with no batch yet (`donation.batch_id` NULL is the entire state machine -- there is no status column). Paginated, so `summary` reports the whole unpaid set rather than the page.

200.description: One page of unpaid donations, and the totals for all of them

summary.description: The whole outstanding set, not the page. A batch can only be built from what is on screen, so this is how a second page makes itself known.

400.description: organizationId missing, or a malformed limit, offset or order

get.description: Admin only, published and unpublished alike -- the public view of the same payouts is GET /api/info/donation, which shows published batches and never users.

200.description: One page of batches, newest transfer first by default

400.description: limit beyond the cap, or a malformed order, organizationId or published

post.description: Admin only. Created unpublished: the batch exists, holds its donations and is invisible until PUT /{id}/publish. `donationIds` is explicit rather than "everything unpaid" -- the admin pays what they saw, and a donation confirmed since the list loaded must not be swept into a transfer that did not cover it. Membership is frozen afterwards, so correcting it means DELETE and rebuild.

201.description: The batch as recorded, unpublished and with no evidence yet

400.description: A transfer date in the future (BATCH_FUTURE_TRANSFER), a donation that does not exist (DONATION_NOT_FOUND), one owed to another foundation (DONATION_ORGANIZATION_MISMATCH) or one already paid (DONATION_ALREADY_BATCHED) -- the code in the body says which

get.summary: Read one batch, with its frozen membership list
get.description: Admin only. The members are what the transfer covered and cannot change.

200.description: The batch, its evidence and its donations

organization.description: null only if the organisation row has gone, which a FK should prevent

transferredAmount.description: What actually left the bank account

transferredAt.description: ISO 8601. The date the money moved, not the date typed in

reference.description: Bank transaction number, or the last account digits

note.description: The internal memo. Deliberately not part of the public record

published.description: Whether the public page shows it

donationCount.description: Members, aggregated on read rather than stored

platformTopUp.description: transferredAmount - donationSubtotal. Signed, deliberately not clamped: a negative value is exactly what PUT /{id}/publish refuses, so hiding it would hide the reason

put.summary: Correct the figures of an unpublished batch
put.description: Admin only, and unpublished only: a published batch is part of the public record. Membership is not editable here -- to fix the wrong set of donations, DELETE the batch, which releases them, and build it again.

400.description: It is published (BATCH_PUBLISHED) or the transfer date is in the future (BATCH_FUTURE_TRANSFER)

delete.description: Admin only, and unpublished only. The only way to correct a wrong membership list: every member goes back to `batch_id` NULL, and the evidence rows and their S3 objects go with it.

400.description: The batch is published (BATCH_PUBLISHED)

post.description: Admin only, and the one write allowed on a published batch: a foundation's receipt and its thank-you letter routinely arrive weeks after the money does, and hiding a real payout again just to append them would be worse. The body carries the file as base64 (with or without a `data:` prefix); it is uploaded to S3 under `donations/{batchId}/` and the row keeps the key.

400.description: A kind that is not UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, an unsupported mimeType, or data that is not base64 or is beyond the size cap

delete.description: Admin only, and unpublished only: removing proof from a published batch would leave the public page asserting a payout it can no longer evidence. The S3 object goes with the row.

400.description: The batch is published (BATCH_PUBLISHED)

404.description: No such batch, or no such evidence on it

put.summary: Make one batch visible on the public page
put.description: Admin only. The guards live here, because GET /api/info/donation reports platformTopUp with its sign on the grounds that an underpaid batch should never have been published: this is the place that has to be true. Evidence is required -- a transparency page with nothing to show is just a claim.

400.description: Already published (BATCH_ALREADY_PUBLISHED), less was transferred than the donations total (BATCH_UNDERPAID), or nothing is attached to show (BATCH_NO_EVIDENCE)

put.description: Admin only. The way back out of a mis-click; the public page lists published only.

400.description: It is not published (BATCH_NOT_PUBLISHED)
